Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(ggmap)
library(leaflet)

API Key

register_stadiamaps("0ca4e2d5-36a9-4a89-ab81-cfc2f0ec1652", write = FALSE)

Load the Data

For this homework, we will use the shark attack data to visualize where the attacks occurred. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

sharks <- read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(longitude !="NA" & latitude !="NA") %>% # pulling out NA locations
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude)) # converting longitude to numeric
  1. Use the range of the latitude and longitude to build an appropriate bounding box for your map.
summary(sharks)

lat <- c(32.59, 41.56)
long <- c(-124.7, -117.1)

bbox <- make_bbox(long, 
                  lat, 
                  f = 0.03)
  1. Load a map from stamen in a terrain style projection and display the map.
map1 <-  get_stadiamap(bbox,
                       maptype = "stamen_terrain",
                       zoom = 7)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
ggmap(map1)

  1. Build a map that overlays the recorded observations of shark attacks in California.
ggmap(map1)+
  geom_point(data=sharks,
             aes(longitude,
                 latitude),
             size = 0.75,
             color = "black",
             alpha = 0.8
             )+
  labs(
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    title = "Shark Attack Locations Across California"
  )

  1. Build a map that only shows the fatalities.
sharks_fatal <- sharks %>% 
  filter(injury == "fatal")

ggmap(map1)+
  geom_point(data=sharks_fatal,
             aes(longitude,
                 latitude),
             size = 0.75,
             color = "black",
             alpha = 0.8
             )+
  labs(
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    title = "Fatal Shark Attack Locations Across California"
  )

  1. Build the same map (fatalities only), but this time make it interactive using leaflet. Also, color the points red.
lon_min = -123.7783     
lon_max = -117.28       
lat_min = 32.855
lat_max = 39.57833      

leaflet(sharks_fatal) %>% 
  addProviderTiles(providers$Stadia.StamenTerrain) %>% 
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    radius = 2,
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    color = "red"
  ) %>% 
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft") %>% 
  fitBounds(
    lng1 = lon_min,
    lat1 = lat_min,
    lng2 = lon_max,
    lat2 = lat_max
  )
  1. Which county has the highest number of recorded shark attacks? Make a map that only shows the attacks in this county. (hint: it may help improve the map if you remove duplicate locations, i.e. multiple attacks at the same location.)
sharks_county <- sharks %>% 
  filter(county == "San Diego")

lat2 <- c(32.59 , 33.37)
long2 <- c(-118.1, -117.1)

bbox2 <- make_bbox(long2, 
                  lat2, 
                  f = 0.03)

map2 <-  get_stadiamap(bbox2,
                       maptype = "stamen_terrain",
                       zoom = 10)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
sharks_county_unique <- sharks_county %>% 
  distinct(latitude, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  distinct(longitude, .keep_all = T)


ggmap(map2)+
  geom_point(data=sharks_county_unique,
             aes(longitude,
                 latitude),
             size = 0.75,
             color = "black",
             alpha = 0.8
             )+
  labs(
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    title = "Shark Attack Locations In San Diego County"
  )
